# ADR-0009: The field catalogue is a versioned JSON file, generated by the `catalogue` command and guarded by the `check` command

- Status: Accepted 2026-11-26 (one-way door: hosts commit catalogue files in this format and run these commands in
  their CI)
- Date: 2026-11-26
- Origin: new in the engine repository (query-engine ticket 02); implements ADR-0002 and ADR-0006
- Deciders: proposed by Claude (Anthropic) as engineer; accepted by the product owner 2026-11-26
- Related: ADR-0002 (fields from the host's definitions), ADR-0003 (plan format), ADR-0007 (start-up check)

## Context

ADR-0002 says the engine's fields come from the host's own field definitions, through a catalogue file the
engine's `catalogue` command generates, and that a `check` command fails when a building column is neither in
the catalogue nor on an exclusion list. It leaves open the file's shape, how the definitions are read, and
where each check runs.

Facts that shape the choice, checked on colouring-core commit `cd5fc563` (2026-11-26):

- The definitions are a TypeScript module, `app/src/frontend/config/data-fields-config.ts`. Each entry of its
  `dataFields` object is keyed by a `buildings` column and has a `category` (a member of the `Category` enum
  in `categories-config.ts`), a `title` and, for fields with a fixed list, `items`. Titles are sometimes
  expressions: `"Area code/" + ccconfig.postcode`, where `ccconfig` is `require('../../cc-config.json')`.
- The module imports other modules and a JSON file and uses an enum, so Node cannot import it as it stands.
- `public.buildings` has 306 columns: text, arrays of text, integers, reals, booleans, dates, JSON and several
  PostgreSQL enum types. 39 have a database default (`0`, `false`, `''`, `'None'`, and the id sequence).
- Some definitions have no `buildings` column (`uprns`, for example), and many columns have no definition.

## Decision

**The file.** One JSON document, `formatVersion` `"1.0.0"` (semantic versioning: a minor version adds,
a major version breaks), with a published JSON Schema, `schemas/catalogue-1.schema.json`:

- `categories`: `key` (the definitions' category slug) and `title`, in the host's display order;
- `fields`: one per queryable `buildings` column, in definition order: `key` (the column name), `category`,
  `title`, `type` (`text`, `integer`, `number` or `boolean`), `multiValued` (the column is an array),
  `allowedValues` (the definition's `items`, or `null` when values are free), and `ambiguity` (`null`, or the
  plain reason a stored value may not be an observation);
- `excludedColumns`: every other `buildings` column, each with a plain `reason`.

**Generation.** `node src/cli.ts catalogue --definitions <data-fields-config.ts> --output <file>` reads
`category`, `title` and `items` statically: it parses the module with a TypeScript parser and evaluates only
literals, string concatenation, template strings, arrays, objects, the module's own constants, the enum it
imports, and `require` of a `.json` file. It never runs the host's code. Anything else stops the command with
the field, file and line. Column types and defaults come from the database named by
`QUERY_ENGINE_DATABASE_URL` (catalogue tables only, through the executor). Output is deterministic, so a host
can regenerate and compare in CI.

- Types map: `int2`/`int4`/`int8` → `integer`; `float4`/`float8`/`numeric` → `number`; `text`, `varchar`,
  `bpchar` and enum types → `text`; `bool` → `boolean`; an array of one of these → that type, multi-valued.
- Excluded, with the reason: a column with no definition; a definition that is per user or structured
  (`fields`, object `items`); dates, JSON and other types plan format 1 cannot compare; `items` that do not
  fit the column's type.
- A column with a database default is marked ambiguous, naming the default, until the host's missing-value
  metadata settles it with evidence (ADR-0002).

**Where it is checked.**

- Start-up (the service and `check`): the file named by `QUERY_ENGINE_CATALOGUE_FILE` must parse, follow the
  schema, have unique keys, known categories, and allowed values of the field's type; every field's column
  must exist in `public.buildings` with a compatible type. Otherwise the service refuses to start.
- `check` only: every `buildings` column must be a field or excluded, and every excluded column must exist.
  A new column fails the host's CI, not a running service.
- `node src/cli.ts check` runs what depends on the host's schema and catalogue: the buildings and footprint
  layout, the catalogue checks above and the guard. It reads `QUERY_ENGINE_DATABASE_URL` and
  `QUERY_ENGINE_CATALOGUE_FILE`, works with any login on a database built from the host's own migrations
  (no engine migrations or engine login needed in CI), and exits 1 on any problem. The engine's migrations and
  the restricted login are the service's start-up check's business (ADR-0007).

## Alternatives considered

| Alternative | What it would have meant | Why not |
|---|---|---|
| Import the module with Node | Run the host's definitions to read them | The module needs a bundler (extensionless imports, an enum, `require` of JSON); it would also run the host's code inside the engine's command |
| Regular expressions over the file | Pick out `category:` and `title:` lines | Breaks on multi-line values, concatenation and comments; no line-accurate errors |
| The TypeScript compiler's API | Parse with `typescript` | The engine's TypeScript 7 offers only an unstable API, and TypeScript 5 at run time is 23 MB |
| Allowed values from the data | `SELECT DISTINCT` per column | Contradicts ADR-0002; values nobody has recorded yet would be missing |
| The guard at start-up too | Refuse to start on an unlisted column | A host migration adding a column would take the engine down on its next restart; CI is where the host can act |
| YAML or TypeScript catalogue | Friendlier to edit | JSON needs no parser beyond the standard library and is what the API serves |

## Consequences

- A host commits its generated catalogue and regenerates it when its definitions or schema change; its CI runs
  `check` (host setup guide).
- Field keys are column names, so plans name columns; renaming a column is a breaking change for saved plans.
- Ambiguity marking is coarse until the missing-value metadata arrives: every defaulted column is ambiguous.
- New setting: `QUERY_ENGINE_CATALOGUE_FILE`, required by the service and `check`.
- New dependency: `@babel/parser` (tools inventory).

## Plain-English summary

The engine keeps the list of building details it can ask about in one file. A command builds that file from the
platform's own definitions of its fields and from the database, without running the platform's code. The
engine will not start if the file is broken or names a detail the database lacks, and a check the platform
runs on every change fails when a new database column has not been added to the list or set aside with a
reason.
